title: India come from behind to beat Pakistan 2-1 and win a record 10th SAFF Championship
dek: Suhail Ahmed Bhat and Sandip Mandi scored after Pakistan, playing in their first final, took the lead in Dhaka. India have now won three titles in a row.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
India won the SAFF Championship for a record 10th time on Tuesday night, beating Pakistan 2-1 in the final at the National Stadium in Dhaka. It was India's third title in a row and their 10th in the tournament's 15 editions, and they went through the competition unbeaten, according to reports.

Pakistan, in their first SAFF final, took the lead through Alamgir Ali Ghazi in first-half stoppage time. Their player Junaid Ahmed Shah was sent off in the 59th minute after a video review for a reckless challenge on Brison Fernandes, and a minute later Suhail Ahmed Bhat equalised, his fourth goal of the tournament. Sandip Mandi headed in Abdul Rabeeh's corner two minutes from the end of normal time to win it, reports said. About 10,000 spectators watched.

After the match the two teams formed guards of honour for each other at the medal ceremony. India's coach, Naushad Moosa, said the players had not been told to do it and that it reflected respect for how Pakistan had played; Pakistan's coach, Nolberto Solano, said the teams were rivals only on the pitch, according to reports.

The India side in Dhaka was separate from the senior squad under Khalid Jamil, which ended a tour of New Zealand with a 3-0 defeat in Christchurch. India had also beaten Pakistan 3-2 in the group stage on 5 November.
